rules.title: California Statewide Rent Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may not increase rent more than 5% plus the local CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period.

coverage_conditions.text: Exemptions include: affordable housing, dorms, units under local rent control with stricter limits, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes), single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate entities with proper notice, duplexes where owner occupies one unit.

rules.exemptions: Housing subject to rent control with lower caps is exempt; single-family homes and condos owned by individuals/non-corporate entities are exempt if proper notice provided; owner-occupied duplexes exempt.
rules.interaction: Yields to the listed local rules where they cover the building (state rule becomes superseded).
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act - Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy, landlords cannot terminate a tenancy without stating a just cause reason in the written notice.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential real property after tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if additional adults added). Exemptions include: transient/tourist hotels, certain institutional housing, dormitories, owner-occupied housing with shared facilities, single-family owner-occupied with ≤2 units, duplex owner-occupied, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes), certain alienable properties owned by individuals (not REITs/corporations), affordable housing.

rules.exemptions: Exempt: buildings with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); single-family owner-occupied residences with ≤2 units; duplex owner-occupied; owner-occupied with shared bathroom/kitchen; alienable properties owned by natural persons (not REITs/corporations); affordable housing; transient hotels; institutional housing; dormitories. Local ordinances more protective apply instead.
rules.interaction: Yields to the listed local rules where they cover the building (state rule becomes superseded).
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy

rules.title: Security deposit limit – one month's rent for most landlords
rules.requirement: Most landlords in California may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit for both furnished and unfurnished units starting July 1, 2024.

coverage_conditions.text: many landlords

rules.exemptions: Small landlords (two properties, no more than four residential units total, natural person/family trust/LLC with natural person members) can charge up to two months' rent
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Security deposit limit – one month's rent (general rule)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot demand or receive a security deposit greater than one month's rent, plus first month's rent, except in certain situations.

coverage_conditions.text: rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant

rules.exemptions: Exceptions for advance payments of 6+ months' rent (for leases 6+ months), structural/decorative alterations, service members with higher deposits (refundable after 6 months), and small landlords (natural persons/LLCs owning ≤2 properties with ≤4 total units, who may charge up to 2 months' rent except for service members).
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

rules.title: Security deposit limit – two months' rent for small landlords
rules.requirement: Small landlords who are natural persons or LLCs with natural person members and who own no more than two properties with a total of four or fewer units may charge up to two months' rent as a security deposit.

coverage_conditions.text: landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to service members; landlords cannot refuse to rent to service members because they cannot charge service members the higher two-month deposit. Family trusts included in definition of natural person.
rules.quoted_span:
Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:
(i) The landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons.
(ii) The
landlord owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent

rules.title: Deductions limited to damages beyond ordinary wear and tear
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot deduct from the security deposit for preexisting damage, ordinary wear and tear, or the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear.

coverage_conditions.text: rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant

rules.exemptions: Professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning cannot be charged unless reasonably necessary to return premises to inception condition exclusive of ordinary wear and tear.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies

rules.title: Application screening fee cap and requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee of no more than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI increases since January 1, 1998.

coverage_conditions.text: residential property

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998

rules.title: Source of Income Discrimination Prohibition
rules.requirement: Housing providers in California cannot discriminate against tenants based on their source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, SSI benefits, rental assistance programs, or wages.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most providers of housing and services related to housing such as landlords, tenant screening companies, real estate agents, home sellers, builders, mortgage lenders, and housing authorities

rules.exemptions: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job

rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in housing
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate against or harass tenants or applicants because of their source of income.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to any housing accommodation

rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful:
(a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person

rules.title: Criminal history screening restrictions - blanket bans and arrest-only records prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot impose blanket bans on applicants with criminal records and cannot consider arrests without convictions when screening tenants.
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council regulations (effective Jan. 1, 2020)
rules.quoted_span: The California regulations include limits on what type of criminal history may be sought, how an applicant’s criminal history can be considered, and what actions a landlord may take based on an applicant’s criminal history. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions

rules.title: Credit history screening restrictions for voucher holders (SB 267)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot use credit history in screening applicants with government rental subsidies unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay their rent portion.
rules.citation: SB 267, amending Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quoted_span: last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent

rules.title: Source of income discrimination - Section 8 vouchers protected (SB 329)
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from refusing to participate in government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers.
rules.citation: SB 329 (2019), amending Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quoted_span: In 2019, the California Legislature adopted SB 329, which updated the definition of “source of income” used in the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) to include government housing subsidy programs, such as Section 8. This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs

rules.title: Prohibition on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms in restraint of trade
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to any person (as defined in Section 16702, excluding end consumers) using or distributing common pricing algorithms

rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are excluded from the definition of 'person'
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter

rules.title: Rooming and Boarding Houses: Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good cause and notice requirements of the Anti-Eviction Act when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards.

coverage_conditions.text: Buildings having at least two living units occupied by persons unrelated to each other without private kitchens and bathrooms, with certain exceptions (hotels with >85% temporary occupancy, school/college dormitories, buildings housing only college students, certain residences for the disabled).

rules.exemptions: Owner must give at least three working days' notice to County Welfare Board before starting eviction action for any resident.
rules.quoted_span:
The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the 
Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, 
require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements 
of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Just Cause Requirement
rules.requirement: The Anti-Eviction Act requires just cause for eviction in most residential rental properties in New Jersey.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (with exceptions for occupants with no alternate residence).

rules.exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel/motel/guest house transient or seasonal tenants (except occupants with no alternate residence). Does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member who permanently occupies it.
rules.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family 
homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes

rules.title: Proper Notice for Rent Increase Eviction
rules.requirement: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, the landlord must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.quoted_span:
This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase

rules.title: Anti-Retaliation Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot evict, substantially alter a lease, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising their rights, including enforcing lease or legal rights, making good faith complaints to government authorities, or organizing tenant organizations.

coverage_conditions.text: All rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings. Tenant must have notified landlord in writing and given reasonable time to correct violation before making complaint to government authority.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

rules.title: Landlord Registration Required to Evict
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant if the landlord has not properly registered the rental property as required by law.

coverage_conditions.text: A landlord who owns a one or two-family non-owner-occupied home is required by law to file a registration statement with the clerk of the municipality in which the building is located. If the building has three (3) or more units, the statement must be filed with the Bureau of Housing Inspection

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family homes are not required to be registered.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord 
registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not 
been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37)

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit
rules.requirement: Landlords must return the security deposit plus interest, less any deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant

rules.title: Maximum security deposit limit
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot require a security deposit of more than one and one-half months' rent for residential rental property.

coverage_conditions.text: real property used for dwelling purposes

rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes

rules.title: Truth in Renting Act - Distribution Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must distribute the Truth in Renting Statement to tenants within 30 days after it is posted on the Department website and provide it to new tenants at or before lease execution.

coverage_conditions.text: The Act calls for distribution of the statement by the landlord to all tenants with a rental term of at least one month living in residences with more than two dwelling units, or more than three if the landlord occupies one of the units.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to hotels, motels, or other guest houses serving transient or seasonal tenants, or to owner-occupied buildings of three or fewer units
rules.quoted_span:
Every landlord subject to the Truth in Renting Act, (N.J.S.A. 46:8-43 to 51), hereinafter 
the Act, is required to distribute one copy of the Truth in Renting Statement to each of their tenants 
within 30 days after it has been posted by the Department on its website and shall thereafter provide 
a copy of the most current statement to each new tenant at or prior to the time the tenant executes 
a lease for the rental unit

rules.title: Residential rental property application fee limit
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge more than $50 as an application fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property.

coverage_conditions.text: Does not apply to dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent, or to real estate licensees (unless the licensee is the landlord).

rules.exemptions: Exempts one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; exempts real estate licensees unless they are the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50

rules.title: Source of Lawful Income Protection – Housing
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot discriminate against tenants or purchasers based on their source of lawful income, including Section 8 vouchers.

coverage_conditions.text: All property including open land, whether for business or residential purposes, with exceptions for certain owner-occupied dwellings and religious organization preferences.

rules.exemptions: Exemptions include: rental of single apartment in two-family dwelling where owner occupies other unit; rental of rooms in one-family dwelling occupied by owner; religious organization preferences; housing for older persons (familial status protection only).
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income

rules.title: Source of Income Anti-Discrimination
rules.requirement: It is illegal for landlords or rental agencies to discriminate in renting based on source of lawful income, among other protected characteristics.

coverage_conditions.text: The law applies to all landlord-tenant relationships, except those involving two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.

rules.exemptions: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings, rooms in owner or resident-occupied single home, and single-sex residences (with respect to familial status).
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Criminal History Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers cannot inquire about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer of housing, except for certain drug and sex offender convictions.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to rental dwelling units except dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied properties with 4 or fewer units are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Residential landlords cannot use algorithmic software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents, and software providers cannot use such software to coordinate pricing among competing landlords.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential rental property owners; exemptions include spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs.

rules.exemptions: Does not prohibit spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs.
rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices. It also prohibits software providers and other "coordinators" from using such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords
rules.conflict_note: not yet effective state rule in the same category as in-force local rules (Hoboken, NJ, Jersey City, NJ); flagged for human review.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases would have been capped at the lesser of the CPI increase or 5%, with exemptions for owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, and certain other properties.

coverage_conditions.text: most residential rental units, with exemptions for owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes

rules.exemptions: Exemptions include owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%. The petition included several exemptions, including owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes

rules.title: General prohibition on municipal rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns are prohibited from enacting or enforcing rent control, except that municipalities accepting this chapter may adopt rent control that becomes voluntary for property owners after six months.
rules.exemptions: Property owners with fewer than ten rental units are exempt; units with fair market rent exceeding $400 are exempt; compliance is voluntary after six months; municipality must compensate owners from general funds for the difference between fair market rent and controlled rent.
rules.quoted_span:
No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
(a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord must give fourteen days' written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease, but the tenant can cure by paying all rent due with interest and costs by the answer date.

coverage_conditions.text: written lease

rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit

rules.title: Notice requirements to terminate estate at will
rules.requirement: A landlord or tenant may terminate an at-will tenancy with three months' written notice, or if rent is paid more frequently than every three months, notice equal to the interval between rent payments or thirty days (whichever is longer).
rules.key_value: 3 months or interval between rent payments (min 30 days)
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer

rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection for tenants reporting violations or organizing
rules.requirement: Landlords who retaliate against tenants for reporting code violations, exercising legal rights, or organizing tenant unions are liable for damages of one to three months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater), plus costs and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater

coverage_conditions.text: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.

rules.quoted_span: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law, regulation, by-law or ordinance, which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or exercising the tenant's rights pursuant to section one hundred and twenty-four D of chapter one hundred and sixty-four; or reporting to the board of health or, in the city of Boston to the commissioner of housing inspection or to any other board having as its objective the regulation of residential premises a violation or a suspected violation of any health or building code or of any other municipal by-law or ordinance, or state or federal law or regulation which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or reporting or complaining of such violation or suspected violation in writing to the landlord or to the agent of the landlord; or for organizing or joining a tenants' union or similar organization, or for making or expressing an intention to make, a payment of rent to an organization of unit owners pursuant to paragraph (c) of section six of chapter one hundred and eighty-three A shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee

rules.title: Security deposit maximum and payment limits at commencement of tenancy
rules.requirement: At the start of a tenancy, a landlord cannot require more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and key/lock costs.

coverage_conditions.text: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to vacation/recreational leases of 100 days or less
rules.quoted_span:
At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

rules.title: Last month's rent interest payment requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords who receive last month's rent in advance must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year or the lesser amount received from the bank where the deposit is held.
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor or his agent who receives said rent in advance for the last month of tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held

rules.title: Security deposit interest payment requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords holding a security deposit for one year or longer must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year or the lesser amount received from the bank, payable at the end of each year of tenancy.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy

rules.title: Broker application fee requirements
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge application fees to prospective tenants if they comply with board of registration regulations, including written disclosure requirements.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to licensed brokers only; broker must provide written notice of fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether contingent on lease execution at first personal meeting with applicant

rules.exemptions: Broker must hold valid license; landlord-brokers likely cannot charge fees when acting as landlord
rules.quoted_span: The board’s regulations set out certain detailed requirements, including the steps that a licensed broker must take when dealing with prospective tenants (254 C.M.R. 7)

rules.title: Broker fees must be paid by party who contracted with broker
rules.requirement: A broker fee for finding rental housing can only be paid by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the broker.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord application fees and pre-tenancy charges
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge application fees or any other pre-tenancy charges except first month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit, and lock-change fee.
rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers may charge application fees under 254 CMR 7
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B)

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibition - public assistance recipients
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to discriminate in housing, credit, or services against individuals receiving public assistance or housing subsidies because of their recipient status or program requirements.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination based on sealed or expunged criminal records
rules.requirement: Employers may not request or use certain criminal history information, including non-conviction records, old first-offense misdemeanors, misdemeanor convictions over 3 years old (if no recent convictions), or sealed/expunged records, in employment decisions.
rules.quoted_span: For an employer, himself or through his agent, in connection with an application for employment, or the terms, conditions, or privileges of employment, or the transfer, promotion, bonding, or discharge of any person, or in any other matter relating to the employment of any person, to request any information, to make or keep a record of such information, to use any form of application or application blank which requests such information, or to exclude, limit or otherwise discriminate against any person by reason of his or her failure to furnish such information through a written application or oral inquiry or otherwise regarding: (i) an arrest, detention, or disposition regarding any violation of law in which no conviction resulted, or (ii) a first conviction for any of the following misdemeanors: drunkenness, simple assault, speeding, minor traffic violations, affray, or disturbance of the peace, or (iii) any conviction of a misdemeanor where the date of such conviction or the completion of any period of incarceration resulting therefrom, whichever date is later, occurred 3 or more years prior to the date of such application for employment or such request for information, unless such person has been convicted of any offense within 3 years immediately preceding the date of such application for employment or such request for information, or (iv) a criminal record, or anything related to a criminal record, that has been sealed or expunged pursuant to chapter 276

rules.title: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: This bill would address algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market.
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.conflict_note: pending state rule in the same category as in-force local rules (Boston, MA); flagged for human review.

rules.title: Annual rent increase limit at lease expiration or termination
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or termination, rent increases are capped at 5% or the CPI percentage difference for the lease period, whichever is less.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less

rules.title: Tax surcharge for property taxes
rules.requirement: Landlords may seek a tax surcharge from tenants for municipal property tax increases above the 1988 tax year or the year the landlord acquired the property, whichever is later.
rules.exemptions: Rental units must be registered to qualify for a tax surcharge
rules.quoted_span: For any application for a tax surcharge after the effective date of this chapter, a landlord may seek a tax surcharge to be charged to a tenant because of an increase in municipal property taxes if said taxes are in excess of those assessed for the year that the landlord acquired the property or for the 1988 tax year, whichever assessment date is later

rules.title: Water and sewerage surcharge
rules.requirement: Landlords may seek a water and sewer surcharge from tenants for increases in municipal water and sewer charges above those assessed for 1996.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may seek a water and sewerage surcharge from a tenant because of an increase in the municipal water and sewer charges in excess of those assessed for 1996

rules.title: Capital improvement surcharge
rules.requirement: Landlords may apply to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a rental surcharge for capital improvements to the building or individual units.
rules.exemptions: The dwelling must be in compliance with housing maintenance, building, fire and other applicable City codes, and not subject to a City-held title lien
rules.quoted_span: Upon notice to its tenants, a landlord may apply to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a rental surcharge for capital improvement to the building and/or demised premises

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords in Hoboken are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices or lease terms.

coverage_conditions.text: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken

rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing. For purposes of this chapter, "price fixing using algorithmic pricing" shall be defined as the use of software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other real estate lessors in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units among competing real estate lessors
rules.conflict_note: State rule r-0026 (P.L. 2026, c. 43) is not yet effective in the same category; possible conflict or preemption, flagged for human review.

rules.title: New Construction Exemption (up to 30 years or mortgage amortization)
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from rent control for up to 30 years or the amortization period of the initial mortgage, whichever is less.

coverage_conditions.text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings with Certificate of Occupancy issued after the effective date.

rules.exemptions: Landlord must apply to the Board for exemption certification with Certificate of Occupancy before occupancy; exemption period begins on first day of occupancy or 30 days after application, whichever occurs first.
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less

rules.title: Vacant Property Exemption (5 years after substantial rehabilitation)
rules.requirement: Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months are exempt from rent control for five years if the landlord rehabilitates them at a cost exceeding 50% of fair market value and obtains a Certificate of Occupancy.

coverage_conditions.text: Dwellings vacant for minimum 18 months and substantially rehabilitated.

rules.exemptions: Landlord must submit appraisal, rehabilitation plan, permits, and Certificate of Occupancy; application must be submitted within 2 years of acquiring first permit; landlord must notify tenants 90 days before exemption expires.
rules.quoted_span: Dwellings which become vacant and remain vacant for a minimum of 18 months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period has exceeded 50% of the fair market value of the dwelling and that the dwelling has received a Certificate of Occupancy and meets all applicable State and municipal health and housing codes

rules.title: Maximum Annual Increase 25% Cap
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board may not grant rent increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to any tenant subject to rent control.

rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant

rules.title: Annual Rent Increase Cap (CPI-based, max 4%)
rules.requirement: Rent increases are limited to the percentage increase in the CPI-U for the New York–northern New Jersey–Long Island area (15 months prior to 3 months prior to increase), with a maximum cap of 4% per year.

coverage_conditions.text: All multiple dwellings as defined in subsection 19:2-2 are subject to Rent Control.

rules.exemptions: Exemptions include public housing, hotels/motels for transients, commercial rentals, newly constructed multiple dwellings for up to 30 years or amortization period (whichever is less), vacant dwellings substantially rehabilitated (5 years), and units under certain governmental contracts.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%

rules.title: Frequency Limit on Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Rent for any unit may not be increased more than once in any consecutive twelve‑month period, regardless of tenant turnover or change of ownership.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to any housing space subject to rent control.

rules.quoted_span: The rents for any housing space shall not be increased more than the percentages stated above in any consecutive twelve-month period irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying the housing space during the twelve-month period, any change of ownership of the landlord or vacancy of the housing space

rules.title: Substantial Compliance and Registration Required for Increases
rules.requirement: No rent increase or surcharge is allowed unless the dwelling is free of code violations and the landlord has registered with the Rent Control Office.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all dwellings subject to rent control.

rules.exemptions: Substantial compliance means free from violations of State and Newark health, safety, building, property maintenance, and fire safety codes.
rules.quoted_span: No annual rent increase, major new improvement surcharge, tax surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or has not met registration requirements as specified in subsection 19:2-9.8

rules.title: Definition of Rent Includes Security Deposits
rules.requirement: Rent is defined to include security deposits, damage deposits, and cleaning deposits demanded or received in connection with occupancy of housing space.

coverage_conditions.text: All housing spaces subject to rent control.

rules.exemptions: This is a definitional provision included within rent control; state law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 et seq.) separately governs security deposit amounts and handling.
rules.quoted_span: Shall mean the consideration and shall include any bonus, benefits or gratuity demanded or received for or, in connection with, the use or occupancy of housing space or the transfer of a lease of such housing spaces, including, but not limited to monies demanded or paid for parking, pets, the use of furniture, subletting, security deposits and damage and cleaning deposits

rules.title: Ban the Box - Criminal History Inquiry Restrictions in Housing
rules.requirement: Landlords and real estate brokers may not inquire about or consider an applicant's criminal history until after the applicant submits a formal application.

coverage_conditions.text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application

rules.title: Ban the Box - Prohibition on Criminal History References in Housing Advertisements
rules.requirement: Landlords and real estate brokers may not produce or disseminate any advertisement that directly or indirectly references the use or consideration of an applicant's criminal history.

coverage_conditions.text: Article does not apply to rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling. Exception for statutory eligibility restrictions specified by law.
rules.quoted_span: In connection with any rental, lease, or sublease, it shall be unlawful for a landlord or real estate broker to produce or disseminate any advertisement that directly or indirectly references the use or consideration of an applicant's criminal history

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: This bill would have authorized the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources when starting the eviction process or when not renewing a lease, delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.

coverage_conditions.text: The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston. The only exempt properties are residences: 1. in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and 2. in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.

rules.exemptions: Exempt properties are residences in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, health facilities, or non-profit facilities providing short-term treatment for substance abuse.
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy
agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: This bill would have authorized the city of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - Criminal History Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving City funding or land, or with BPDA inclusionary units, may not consider arrests without conviction, convictions with judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when screening tenants.

coverage_conditions.text: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy

rules.exemptions: Restrictions do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, or to current criminal behavior. Federal or state law preempts this policy.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span:
The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when 
determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: 
 
a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion 
programs, and similar non-convictions. 
b) Convictions that are subject to a form of judicial relief, such as expungement, sealing, 
and certificates for relief from disabilities. 
c) Juvenile records 
d) A conviction more than 5 years old

rules.title: Prohibition of source-of-income discrimination
rules.requirement: It is illegal to discriminate against tenants based on rental assistance (such as Section 8 vouchers) when renting housing in Boston.

rules.title: Prohibition on algorithmic rent coordination services in Philadelphia
rules.requirement: Philadelphia prohibits algorithmic rent coordination practices and allows aggrieved persons to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus equitable relief and attorney fees.
rules.quoted_span: Philadelphia’s ordinance permits an aggrieved person to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, together with equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs
rules.conflict_note: State rule r-0041 (S.2983) is pending in the same category; possible conflict or preemption, flagged for human review.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic and AI-driven rent pricing software
rules.requirement: The city council passed a policy order to ban property management companies from using algorithmic and AI-driven software to set rents.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential property management companies in Cambridge

rules.citation: Policy order passed by Cambridge City Council on June 21, 2026
rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent
